title: CompTIA Security+ vs CySA+: Which First?
subtitle: Which cybersecurity cert to take, and in what order

pros: The most requested entry-level security cert in junior job postings.
Covers the whole foundation: threats, cryptography, IAM, architecture, governance.
A DoD 8570/8140 baseline — the key to many US security contracts.
An implicit prerequisite for nearly everything else in cyber.
cons: Broad but shallow: it doesn't prove analyst skills.
Mixes multiple choice and performance-based questions (PBQs) — don't underestimate the prep.
certs.bestFor: You're new to cybersecurity — it's the first cert to put on your résumé.

pros: Blue-team focused: detection, threat hunting, analytics, MITRE ATT&CK.
The CompTIA cert closest to a SOC analyst's real day-to-day.
Recognized for analyst / tier-1 and tier-2 SOC roles.
The logical follow-up to Security+ in the CompTIA pathway.
cons: Assumes you already have the Security+ fundamentals.
Too specialized to serve as your very first cert.
Same price as Security+ ($404) for a narrower audience.
certs.bestFor: You already have the basics (or Security+) and are targeting a SOC analyst role.

verdicts.why: Security+ is the foundation. Tackling CySA+ without the basics is putting the roof on before the walls.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting a SOC analyst job within 12 months.
verdicts.why: CySA+ matches an analyst's daily work: alert triage, detection, threat hunting.

verdicts.profile: You want to open the most doors in job postings.
verdicts.why: Security+ appears in far more junior postings — it's the most common HR filter in cyber.

verdicts.profile: You already have Security+ and want the logical next step.
verdicts.why: That's exactly the progression CompTIA designed: a generalist foundation, then analyst specialization.

tldr: Security+ first, always. CySA+ next, once you're actually targeting a SOC role.
